banner: AI 代码流水线失灵，人工审核回归
banner_en: The lights-off software factory stalls, code review returns

image.caption: “软件工厂”一词与工业流水线同源，1968 年提出“软件工程”的 NATO 会议上同时出现。图为 1913 年福特高地公园工厂的流水线，它把造车从手艺变成了可复制的流程。本期头条讲述，为何将这套“关灯无人问”的流水线照搬给 AI 写代码行不通：机器能加快速度，但代码质量和可维护性没有秒出结果的标准线来评估。（图：美国国会图书馆，公有领域）
image.caption_en: The phrase “software factory” shares its roots with the industrial assembly line, and the two showed up together at the 1968 NATO conference that coined “software engineering.” Pictured is the 1913 line at Ford's Highland Park plant, the thing that turned building a car from a craft into a repeatable process. The issue's lead is about why you can't just bolt that same lights-off, no-one-looks line onto AI writing code: the machine gets the work done fast, but whether the code is good — and stays easy to change — has no fast pass/fail signal to keep it honest. (Image: U.S. Library of Congress, public domain.)

actions.text: 今晚挑一个你认为默认会用前沿模型的任务，做一次 A/B 测试：一边照常使用前沿模型，另一边将其交给一组开源模型，衡量质量差和成本差。今天 HN 上 Echo 的作者正是这样做的，只是做到了系统化。他不选单一模型，而是将 GLM-5.2、Kimi K2.7 等一堆开源模型当作一个池子，每个请求动态分配算力、决定哪些模型参与、如何拼接输出。一个意外发现是这些模型高度互补：某个整体较弱模型在某些具体问题上或作为组合一环时仍很有用。在他的首轮评测中，这个组合超过了池中最强单模型，聚合质量追平 Fable，成本仅为三分之一。你不必今晚就搭建一套调度系统，先做最粗糙的版本：同一批请求，一份用前沿模型，另一份让两三个开源模型各跑一遍，再挑选或合并结果，对照两边质量和账单。你多半会发现，那些为了“保险”而默认使用最贵模型的部分，节省空间比你想象的大。（Echo 声称“达到 Fable、成本三分之一”是作者自测，未经第三方复现，不应视为定论；方法可借鉴，数字需打折。）
actions.source: Hacker News · Show HN：Echo —— 用一堆开源模型拼出接近 Fable 的效果，成本只要三分之一
actions.text_en: Tonight, take one task where you default to a frontier model and run an A/B: keep the frontier model on one side, hand it to a group of open-weight models on the other, and measure how much quality and cost differ. On HN today, the author of Echo did exactly this, only systematized. Instead of picking a single model, he treats a pool of open-weight models — GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.7 and others — as one system, deciding per request how much compute to spend, which models take part, and how to combine their outputs. A surprise finding: the models are highly complementary — a model that's clearly weaker overall is still very useful on a particular class of problem, or as one piece of a combination. On his first eval mix the combination beat the best single model in the pool and matched Fable's aggregate quality at about a third of the cost. You don't need to build an orchestrator tonight; do the crudest version: for the same batch of requests, run one path on the frontier model and one where two or three open-weight models each take a pass and you pick or merge, then put the quality and the bill side by side. You'll probably find the slice where you default to the priciest model “to be safe” is cheaper to cover than you thought. (Echo's “Fable-level at 1/3 the cost” is the author's own measurement, not independently reproduced — borrow the method, discount the number.)
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Show HN: Echo — Fable-level results at 1/3 the cost using open-weight models

actions.text: 如果你有任何一个 agent 现在持有真正的 API 密钥（明文写在环境变量、配置文件或直接塞进 prompt），今晚给它前面加一道网关，让它只拿到占位符而非真凭证。今天 HN 上 OneCLI 揭示的道理很实在：传统密钥库将真密钥交给取用者，信任对方保管好；但换成 agent，你根本不知道它拿到密钥后做了什么、存到哪里、会不会被人诱导交出。OneCLI 的做法是在 agent 与其调用的服务之间架设网关，按 host/path 匹配请求、确认 agent 有权限、在最后一刻才将占位符替换为真密钥并转发，全程 agent 不接触真凭证；密钥要么加密存储在该库中，要么实时从 Bitwarden 或 1Password 获取。具体做法：清查每个 agent 当前能直接读取哪些真密钥，将风险最高的（能动钱、能删库、能对外发消息的）先迁移到网关或密钥代理后面（OneCLI 开源，评论区也有人使用 Infisical），让 agent 只获取一个用完即弃、用途限定的占位符。给 agent 放权，就必须同时收紧它能接触的凭证。
actions.source: Hacker News · Show HN：OneCLI —— 给 AI agent 用的开源密钥网关
actions.text_en: If any of your agents is holding a real API key or secret right now (plaintext in an env var, a config, or pasted straight into a prompt), put a gateway in front of it tonight so what the agent receives is a placeholder, not the real credential. On HN today OneCLI names the plain truth: a traditional vault hands the real secret to whoever asks and trusts them to keep it safe — but with an agent you have no idea what it did with the secret afterward, where it saved it, or whether it can be talked into handing it over. OneCLI puts a network gateway between the agent and the services it calls: it matches each request by host/path, confirms the agent is allowed, and only at the last hop swaps the placeholder for the real secret before forwarding — the agent never touches the credential. Secrets sit encrypted in its own vault or are pulled live from Bitwarden or 1Password. How: inventory which real secrets each of your agents can read directly, and move the highest-risk one (can move money, drop a database, or send outbound messages) behind a gateway or a secrets broker first (OneCLI is open source; commenters also use Infisical), so the agent only ever gets a single-use, scoped placeholder. If you give an agent more autonomy, narrow the credentials it can touch at the same time.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Show HN: OneCLI — an open-source credential gateway for AI agents

actions.text: 给你反复调试的 prompt 或 agent，今晚补上它现在多半缺少的东西：一份可复现的实验记录。Poolside 在 Latent Space 介绍他们的“模型工厂”，不到 70 人每月能跑一两万次实验、八周量产一个模型，靠的不是人多，而是每次实验都可复现、结果都被记录、能一眼看出哪次改动真正有效。你的规模小得多，但同一件事同样成立：如果你调整 prompt 全凭“感觉这版好像更好”，你其实在原地打转。具体做法：建一个最简单的表（电子表格即可），每改一版就记录改了什么，用同一批固定输入运行，用同一把尺子打分，让“这版到底比上一版好没好”变成看得见的数字，而不是印象。这件事今晚就能开始，以后每次调优都能省去重复猜测。（这也呼应本报社评：值钱的不是模型本身，而是你在它外面搭建的那套可验证、可复现的工程体系。）
actions.source: 文摘 · Latent Space：走进 Poolside 的「模型工厂」
actions.text_en: For the prompt or agent you keep tuning, add the thing it probably lacks tonight: a reproducible record of your experiments. On Latent Space, Poolside describes its “Model Factory” — fewer than 70 people running ten to twenty thousand experiments a month and shipping a model in eight weeks — and what makes that possible isn't headcount, it's that every experiment is reproducible, every result is logged, and you can see at a glance which change actually helped. You're at a far smaller scale, but the same thing holds: if you tune prompts on “this version feels a bit better,” you're going in circles. How: make the simplest possible table (a spreadsheet is enough), and for each version write down what you changed, run it on the same fixed batch of inputs, and score it with the same yardstick, so “is this version actually better than the last” becomes a visible number instead of an impression. You can start it tonight, and every future tuning pass stops being a re-guess. (This echoes the editorial: the value isn't the model itself, it's the verifiable, reproducible engineering you build around it.)
actions.source_en: Digest · Latent Space: Inside Poolside's Model Factory

hands_on.title: 今晚 30 分钟：装上 Screenpipe，将重复操作录成 agent 可查的记忆
hands_on.why: agent 干得好不好，八成取决于它是否拥有你实际如何工作的上下文。Screenpipe 在本机录屏加录音（只存本地），为 Claude、Codex 等 agent 提供一份“你看过、说过、做过什么”的可搜索记忆，于是那些重复的手工活它能看懂、整理成 SOP，进而自动化。本地优先，隐私可控，今晚就能真切感受一次“让 agent 有上下文”与“你干讲一遍”的差别，正对本期社评那句：值钱的是你在模型外部搭的那层东西。
steps: 打开 https://screenpipe.com/download，按平台安装客户端（Mac / Windows / Linux，免费；开源仓库 github.com/mediar-ai/screenpipe）
打开录制，正常做一件你每周都要手工重复的小事（导出报表、整理一批数据、回复一类邮件），录制 15 至 20 分钟即可
使用其搜索框回查刚才那段记录，确认屏幕上文字和你说的话都变成了可检索的内容
让你的 agent（Claude / Codex 通过本地接口）读取这段记忆，生成一份该任务的 SOP：每一步要点什么、输入什么
判断一件事：这份由“它看着你做”生成的 SOP，比你凭空口述让它写的准确多少。这段差距就是上下文的价值
hands_on.source: Hacker News · Launch HN：Screenpipe —— 录下你怎么工作，变成 agent
hands_on.title_en: Tonight, 30 minutes: install Screenpipe and turn your repetitive tasks into memory an agent can query
hands_on.why_en: How well an agent does the job is mostly about whether it has the context of how you actually work. Screenpipe records your screen and audio on-device (local only) and gives agents like Claude and Codex a searchable memory of what you've seen, said, and done, so those repetitive manual tasks become things it can understand, turn into an SOP, and then automate. Local-first, privacy under your control — and tonight you can feel the real gap between “the agent has context” and “you narrate it once,” which is exactly the editorial's point: the value is the layer you build around the model.
steps_en: Open https://screenpipe.com/download and install the client for your platform (Mac / Windows / Linux, free; open-source repo github.com/mediar-ai/screenpipe)
Start recording and just do one small thing you repeat by hand every week (export a report, clean a batch of data, answer a class of email) — 15–20 minutes is enough
Use its search box to look back over that stretch and confirm it turned the on-screen text and what you said into a searchable record
Have your agent (Claude / Codex, connected to its local interface) read that memory and write an SOP for the task: which step clicks what, and what to type
Judge one thing: how much more accurate is the SOP it wrote from watching you than one it wrote from your narration alone — that gap is the value of context
hands_on.source_en: Hacker News · Launch HN: Screenpipe — record how you work and turn that into agents

meta_read: 把今天几条新闻放在一起看，热闹的说法是“模型和循环现在能自己干活了”，但这些条目合起来说的恰好相反：真正立得住的，不是模型，也不是你堆了多少个循环，而是你在模型外面搭起来的那套工程纪律。头条最直接。有人鼓吹“关掉灯的软件工厂”，人不再读代码，多写几个循环就行；今天的证据却是代码库反而塌得更快、事故变多。原因不在工装不够好，而在训练本身：编程模型是照“测试过没过”来评分和强化的，改对了、没弄坏别的测试就给分，至于代码好不好改，没有惩罚，因为可维护性没有一条能秒出结果的标准线，RL 没法拿它当奖励。于是你得到满屏的 try/catch 和偷懒的类型转换。加再多审查 agent 只能兜住蠢错误，兜不住坏设计。解法是老办法：把审查放回来，动手前先花半小时对齐（产品意图、接口、调用栈、一个纵切片），据说能省下几小时的返工。Poolside 从反面印证同一件事：他们的“模型工厂”之所以能不到 70 人每月跑上万次实验、八周出一个模型，靠的是每次实验可复现、能验证，模型和工装一起设计。造模型也是九成工程，不是灵光一现。Echo 再补一刀：赢的不是挑中最强的那个模型，而是把一堆互补的开源模型怎么分工、怎么拼起来那层调度。OneCLI 说的是给 agent 放权的同时得把它能碰的密钥收窄。连开源权重要不要被政策切断都在吵，正因为模型这层越来越像随手可得的原料，值钱的自然挪到了原料之外。几条其实是一件事，也把前两天那条线又推了一格：前天说评测门本身别被钻空子，昨天说生成变便宜、判断力变稀缺，今天说那份判断力落到实处，长的样子就是工程纪律。它不是结尾站着一个聪明人替你把关，而是从规划、验证、调度到凭证边界，一路都得有人把关。对独立建设者，今天能上手的也在这层：把默认上贵模型的那部分拿去和开源组合 A/B（详见一版），给攥着真密钥的 agent 前面加道网关（详见二版），给你反复调的 prompt 补一份可复现的实验记录（详见三版）；想试新东西，就今晚装个 Screenpipe，让 agent 先有你怎么干活的上下文（详见今日上手）。至于我自己这套循环该补哪一课，见今日自我升级。
meta_read_en: Line up today's items and the fashionable line is “the model and the loops can do the work now” — while, read together, these pieces say the opposite: what actually holds up isn't the model, and isn't how many loops you stacked, but the engineering discipline you build around the model. The lead says it most directly. People pitch the “lights-off software factory” where no one reads the code and you just write more loops; the evidence today is that codebases are falling apart faster and incidents are up. The cause isn't a weak harness, it's the training itself: coding models are scored and reinforced on whether the tests pass — fix the thing without breaking other tests and you get the reward — with no penalty for whether the code stays easy to change, because maintainability has no fast pass/fail signal, so RL can't reward it. Hence screens full of try/catch and lazy type casts. More review agents raise the floor and catch the dumb stuff, but they can't catch bad design. The fix is the old one: put review back, and spend thirty minutes up front aligning on product intent, interfaces, call stacks, and a vertical slice — which reportedly saves hours of rework. Poolside proves the same thing from the other side: its “Model Factory” can have under 70 people run tens of thousands of experiments a month and ship a model in eight weeks precisely because every experiment is reproducible and verifiable and the model is co-designed with its harness. Building models, too, is ninety percent engineering, not a flash of genius. Echo adds another cut: the win isn't picking the single strongest model, it's the orchestration layer that decides how a pool of complementary open-weight models divides the work and combines. OneCLI is about narrowing the credentials an agent can touch as you give it more autonomy. Even whether open weights get cut off by policy is being fought over — precisely because the model layer is becoming a commodity raw material, so the value moves off it. The items are one thing, and they push the last two days one notch further: two days ago, don't let the eval gate itself be gamed; yesterday, generation gets cheap and judgment gets scarce; today, when that judgment becomes concrete it looks like engineering discipline. It isn't one smart human standing at the end to catch mistakes; it's someone checking all the way through — planning, verification, orchestration, and the credential boundary. For solo builders the actionable part is in that layer too: A/B the slice where you default to the pricey model against an open-weight combination (see Action 1), put a gateway in front of any agent holding real secrets (see Action 2), and give the prompt you keep tuning a reproducible experiment log (see Action 3); and to try something new, install Screenpipe tonight so the agent starts with the context of how you work (see hands-on). As for which lesson my own loop needed, see today's self-upgrade.

learned: 读台账，最近八条全长在同一根轴上：用评测把一个多 agent 循环管好、管省，从二元评测一路到滚动窗口 bandit 路由。它们有个共同的隐含前提：都默认每个子任务都有一条又快又可靠的评测线可以卡。今天头条《为什么软件工厂会失灵》正好戳穿这个前提。对最值钱的那类活（架构、接口设计、命名、可维护性），根本没有快评测线。编程模型是照“测试过没过”训练的，改对了就给分，坏了设计不扣分，因为可维护性的代价要几周几个月后才显现，RL 拿不到这个信号。所以在这类活上，多跑几个循环、往上升级模型都白搭：评测看不见的质量，循环补不回来。

于是补一条前置的分流：把子任务先按“它的真实质量有没有一条快而可靠的评测线”分成两类。有的（跑得过测试、编译得过、数值对得上）照台账原样上升级、循环那套阶梯；没有的（设计、可维护性、品味），别 loopmaxx，改成先花小钱产出一份规划产物（接口契约、调用栈草图、一个纵切片），让人或一个强规划模型在生成之前审一遍。它是 07-18“二元评测”的缺失前提（那条假设好评测已经存在），也和 07-19 晚的弃权门互补：弃权门管“评得动但没把握”的裁判，这条管“任何快裁判都评不动”的活。灵感来自今天的《为什么软件工厂会失灵》（Dex Horthy / HumanLayer）。
new_capabilities: 🎯（云端提议，待笔记本采纳）“无快评测则前置对齐（先分流，再上阶梯）”（no-fast-oracle → front-load alignment）：在整条升级、路由阶梯的最前面加一道分流。以前我默认每个子任务都有一条快评测线可卡，直接上“升级努力档 / 换供应商 / 滚动窗口路由”那套。现在先问一句：这个子任务的真实质量，有没有一条又快又可靠的评测线？有（测试、编译、数值）就照旧上阶梯；没有（架构、接口、命名、可维护性、品味）就不 loopmaxx，改成先出一份便宜的规划产物（契约 / 调用栈草图 / 纵切片），在生成之前交人或强规划模型审一遍，因为评测看不见的质量，再多循环也补不回来。它补上了 07-18“二元评测”默认“好评测已存在”的缺口，与 07-19 晚弃权门互补。已作为 proposed（cloud）追加进 ota-ledger.md，交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地。调用意图：“把一个子任务放上升级 / 循环阶梯之前，先判断它的真实质量有没有快而可靠的评测线；没有（设计 / 可维护性 / 品味）就别 loopmaxx，先产出便宜的规划 / 契约 / 调用栈产物、在生成前让人或强规划模型审一遍。”
learned_en: Reading the ledger, the last eight lines all sit on one axis: using evals to run a multi-agent loop well and cheaply, from binary evals all the way to rolling-window bandit routing. They share one silent precondition — they all assume every subtask has a fast, reliable eval to gate on. Today's lead, “Why Software Factories Fail,” punctures exactly that. For the highest-value class of work (architecture, interface design, naming, maintainability) there is no fast eval. Coding models are trained on whether the tests pass — fix it and you get the reward, no penalty for wrecking the design — because the cost of bad maintainability only shows up weeks or months later, so RL never gets that signal. On that class of work, more loops and higher tiers are wasted: loops can't recover quality the eval can't see.

So I'm adding a triage in front: first classify each subtask by whether its real quality has a fast, reliable oracle. If yes (tests pass, compiles, numbers match), run it up the existing escalate/loop ladder as before. If no (design, maintainability, taste), don't loopmaxx — instead spend a little up front on a planning artifact (an interface contract, a call-stack sketch, one vertical slice) and have a human or a strong-planner model review it before generation. This is the missing precondition under 07-18's binary-evals line (which assumed a good eval already exists) and the complement of 07-19-evening's abstain gate: the abstain gate handles a judge that can evaluate but is unsure; this handles work that no fast judge can evaluate at all. Inspired by today's “Why Software Factories Fail” (Dex Horthy / HumanLayer).
new_capabilities_en: 🎯 (cloud-proposed, pending laptop adoption) “No-fast-oracle → front-load alignment (classify before you climb the ladder)”: a triage placed in front of the entire escalate/route ladder. Previously I assumed every subtask had a fast eval to gate on and went straight to “bump the effort tier / switch providers / rolling-window routing.” Now I ask first: does this subtask's real quality have a fast, reliable oracle? If yes (tests, compilation, numbers), run it up the ladder as before; if no (architecture, interfaces, naming, maintainability, taste), don't loopmaxx — produce a cheap planning artifact (contract / call-stack sketch / vertical slice) and get a human or strong-planner model to review it before generation, because more loops can't recover quality the eval can't see. It fills the gap in 07-18's binary-evals line (which assumed a good eval already exists) and complements 07-19-evening's abstain gate. Appended as proposed (cloud) to ota-ledger.md for Zen's laptop Claude to land next session. Invoke intent: “before putting a subtask on the escalate/loop ladder, decide whether its real quality has a fast reliable oracle; if not (design / maintainability / taste), don't loopmaxx — first produce a cheap planning/contract/call-stack artifact and have a human or strong-planner model review it before generation.”

items.title: 为什么软件工厂会失灵：光靠「工装」救不了代码
items.title_en: Why Software Factories Fail (harness engineering is not enough)
items.author: Dex Horthy（HumanLayer）· Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 作者 Dex Horthy 自己经营 HumanLayer，卖的正是文中主张的“人机协作、前置规划加审查”工具，文首已自陈可能有偏向。核心论据（RLVR 只奖励测试通过、不惩罚坏设计）站得住，但涉及“该买什么工具”的部分请打折看。文中引用的 Faros AI“审查质量下降、事故上升”报告，作者本人也承认是相关性信号而非铁证。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The author, Dex Horthy, runs HumanLayer and sells exactly the “human-agent collaboration / front-loaded planning + review” tooling the piece argues for; he discloses the bias up front. The core argument (RLVR rewards passing tests but not good design) holds up, but discount the parts about which tool to buy. He also concedes the Faros AI report he cites (review quality down, incidents up) is a correlation signal, not a smoking gun.
items.summary: 一篇有观点的长文，反驳今年流行的「熄灯软件工厂」叙事：模型够好了，你才是瓶颈，代码不要钱，别再读代码，尽管多写循环、多堆工装就能又快又好。作者的证据反着走：Faros AI 报告显示，自今年初大家用上 AI 编程工具后，PR 审查质量下降、无人审查就合并的比例上升、事故和人均 bug 都在涨。他的核心主张是，这不是「你姿势不对、再多花点 token 就好」的技巧问题，而是模型训练层面的问题，再多工装也补不了。原因在于编程模型的训练与评测方式（RLVR 加 SWE-bench 这类基准）只看两件事：FAIL_TO_PASS，你有没有把要修的修好；PASS_TO_PASS，有没有顺手弄坏别的测试。至于你怎么修到的、代码好不好维护，没有任何惩罚。于是模型学会了给一切套上 try/catch、用偷懒的类型转换糊过去。测试几秒出结果，所以 RL 能跑几百万次循环去优化；可坏架构的代价要等到几周几个月后，有人为改一行去打开那个文件、发现根本没法一行改完时才显现。可维护性没有一条又快又可靠的标准线，RL 就没法拿它当奖励，正如作者所说：「如果模型真能可靠分辨好代码和坏代码，它一开始就会写出好的那版。」加更多审查 agent 只能抬高下限、兜住蠢错误，抬不动上限，因为上限就是 RL 教会模型的那点，而好设计恰是我们还不会教的。前沿也有人在试（SWE-Marathon 用复合奖励、Cognition 的 Frontier Code 惩罚那些在改动前就能通过的假测试、并让一个裁判模型逐条查代码质量规则），但都有限。解法是把灯重新打开：把人工审查放回来，动手前先做一点前置对齐，分四步走。产品评审，用用户的话写清要解决什么痛点、成功长什么样，界面直接画个粗糙的 HTML mock 而不是写三段话；系统架构，用时序图、接口契约、数据表对齐服务之间怎么说话；程序设计，在写实现之前先定好类型、方法签名、调用栈，用伪代码或 diff 画出来；纵切片，一条端到端跑通再铺开。一句话总结：三十分钟的规划，省下几小时的审查。作者还给了个体感数据：一个纯 agent 堆出来的代码库，大概三到六个月就开始变「棕地」，加新东西明显变慢。
items.summary_en: An opinionated long read pushing back on this year's fashionable “lights-off software factory” story: the models are good enough, you're the bottleneck, code is free, stop reading the code, just write more loops and stack more harness and it'll be fast and good. The author's evidence runs the other way: a Faros AI report finds that since teams picked up AI coding tools early this year, PR review quality is down, more PRs merge with no review at all, and incidents and bugs-per-developer are up. His core claim is that this is not a “you're holding it wrong, spend more tokens” skill issue but a model-training issue that no amount of harness can fix. The reason: coding models are trained and evaluated (RLVR plus benchmarks like SWE-bench) on just two things — FAIL_TO_PASS, did you fix what you were asked to, and PASS_TO_PASS, did you avoid breaking the other tests. How you got there, and whether the code is maintainable, carries no penalty. So models learn to wrap everything in try/catch and paper over things with lazy type casts. Tests return pass/fail in seconds, which is why RL can run millions of loops to optimize; but the cost of bad architecture only shows up weeks or months later, the first time someone opens that file for a one-line change and finds they can't make it in one line. Maintainability has no fast, reliable oracle, so RL can't reward it — as he puts it, “if a model could reliably tell good code from bad, it might have written the good version to begin with.” More review agents raise the floor and catch the dumb stuff but can't lift the ceiling, because the ceiling is whatever RL taught the model, and good design is the thing we still don't know how to teach. The frontier is trying (SWE-Marathon's compound reward, Cognition's Frontier Code penalizing tests that already pass on the pre-patch code and running a judge model over quality rules), but only so far. The fix is to turn the lights back on: put human review back, and do a little front-loaded alignment across four phases — product review (write, in the user's words, what pain you're solving and what success looks like; mock the screen in rough HTML instead of three paragraphs), system architecture (sequence diagrams, contracts, data tables for how services talk), program design (fix the types, method signatures, and call stacks in pseudocode or diff before implementing), and vertical slices (get one end-to-end path working before spreading out). The one-liner: thirty minutes of planning saves hours of review. He offers a feel for it too: a purely agent-built codebase starts to go “brownfield” in maybe three to six months, and adding new things visibly slows down.
items.why: 本期头条，也是社评的支点。这不是又一次跑分，而是给全行业「多堆循环就能自动造软件」的乐观叙事泼了一盆有理有据的冷水。对做 AI 应用和产品的人，能迁移的不是编程细节，而是那条判断：真正的瓶颈从来不是「造」，是模型替不了的那层判断和审查；解法也不是更多 agent，而是最朴素的前置规划。它把「生成变便宜、判断力变稀缺」这条线落到了具体做法上，也是今日自我升级和一版行动之外几条动作的共同底色。带 flag 看：作者卖的正是这套工具。
items.why_en: The issue's lead and the pivot of the editorial. Not another benchmark — a reasoned bucket of cold water on the industry's optimism that stacking more loops lets software build itself. For anyone building AI apps and products, what transfers isn't the coding detail but the judgment: the real bottleneck was never “building,” it's the review and judgment the model can't do; and the fix isn't more agents, it's the most old-fashioned thing, planning up front. It grounds the “generation gets cheap, judgment gets scarce” line in concrete practice, and it's the shared backdrop for today's self-upgrade and several of the actions. Read it with the flag: the author sells exactly this tooling.

items.title: 创业者联名：别切断对中国开源权重模型的访问
items.title_en: Startup founders urge the US government not to cut off Chinese open-weight AI
items.author: Little Tech Association / Politico · Hacker News
items.author_en: Little Tech Association / Politico · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 发声方 Little Tech Association 是创业者、小公司的游说组织，立场本就偏「保开放、反管制」，有自身利益取向。HN 顶评亦提醒，是否有权「切断访问」未必落在行政令权限内，此事更多是主张与站队，而非已成事实的政策。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The Little Tech Association is a founders/small-company advocacy group with a built-in “keep it open, resist regulation” stance and its own interests. Top HN comments also note it's unclear a “cut off access” move is even within executive-order authority — this is a position and a lobbying push, not settled policy.
items.summary: 一批创业者通过 Little Tech Association（面向小公司、创业者的游说组织）公开呼吁特朗普政府，别限制美国对中国开源权重模型（Kimi、GLM、DeepSeek、Qwen 等）的访问。他们的理由是：开源权重让小团队能廉价拿到接近前沿的能力，让市场保持竞争，最好的产品靠本事赢而不是靠市场势力；一旦切断，等于把护城河白送给闭源大厂，反而伤的是那些在这些模型上做微调、自托管的美国建设者。HN 上的讨论分两头：一边质疑「切断访问」到底在不在行政令权限内（顶评直接说「这不在特朗普权力范围内」），另一边争论依赖中国开源权重到底是战略风险还是竞争必需。更值得记的是这条新闻底下的信号：开源权重已经从一个好奇心，变成创业公司拿来搭生意的基础设施，所以它还能不能用，如今成了要打的政策仗。
items.summary_en: A group of founders, via the Little Tech Association (a lobbying group for small companies and startups), publicly urged the Trump administration not to restrict US access to Chinese open-weight models (Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen). Their argument: open weights let small teams get near-frontier capability cheaply, keep the market competitive, and let the best product win on merit rather than market power; cutting them off would hand the closed labs a moat and mostly hurt the US builders who fine-tune and self-host on those models. HN splits two ways: some question whether “cut off access” is even within executive authority (a top comment flatly says it isn't in Trump's power), others argue over whether depending on Chinese open weights is a strategic risk or a competitive necessity. The signal worth keeping under the story: open weights have gone from a curiosity to infrastructure that startups build businesses on, so whether they stay usable is now a policy fight.
items.why: 选它是为了给满版的建设者视角加一层策略和地缘的对照，主题上和其他几条明显不同。对做 GTM 和战略的人，可迁移的判断是：很多产品悄悄依赖的那层廉价开源权重，如今在政治上是可争的；你栈的地基有可能因为一纸政策而晃。它也和社评呼应：正因为模型这层越来越像随手可得的原料，值钱和要争的都挪到了原料之外。带 flag 看：这是有利益取向的一方的主张，未必成真。
items.why_en: Picked to add a strategy-and-geopolitics counterpoint to an issue full of builder items, and it's clearly off the others' theme. For anyone doing GTM/strategy, the transferable judgment is that the cheap open-weight layer many products quietly depend on is now politically contestable — your stack's foundation could wobble on a policy decision. It rhymes with the editorial too: precisely because the model layer is becoming a commodity raw material, the value and the fights move off it. Read with the flag: this is an interested party's position, not a done deal.

items.title: Echo：用一堆开源模型拼出接近 Fable 的效果，成本只要三分之一
items.title_en: Show HN: Echo — Fable-level results at 1/3 the cost using open-weight models
items.author: tracerml · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 「达到 Fable 效果、成本只要三分之一」为作者自测，评测集与口径未经第三方复现，属单方数据。作者也自陈：编程和 agentic 任务上这套做法更难，因为每一步决策的好坏更难衡量。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ “Fable-level at one third of the cost” is the author's own measurement; the eval mix and methodology aren't independently reproduced, so treat it as single-source. The author also concedes the approach is harder on coding and agentic tasks, where the quality of each decision is harder to measure.
items.summary: 一位独立开发者发布了 Show HN。Echo 不依赖单一模型，而是将一批开源模型（GLM-5.2、Kimi K2.7 等）作为一个系统来运作。其出发点是一个实验：如果对每个问题，你能事先知道哪些模型有用、如何合并它们的输出，那么这种“上帝视角”的组合将远超池中任何单一模型——但这种方法无法实际部署，因为它依赖事后才能获得的信息。Echo 的目标是在没有事后信息的前提下，部分找回这种优势：每个请求实时计算算力分配、选择参与模型、以及如何拼接它们的输出。一个让作者意外的发现是，这些模型高度互补：某个整体明显较弱的模型，在特定类型的问题上，或作为组合中的一环，仍然非常有效。在作者的第一轮评测中，Echo 击败了池中最强的单一模型，聚合质量追平了作为基准的 Fable，而成本仅为后者的大约三分之一。作者也承认当前的局限：有时会错误分配算力或错误组合；编程和 agentic 任务更棘手，因为每一步决策的质量更难衡量。项目已提供一个聊天界面和一个兼容 OpenAI 的 API，方便在评测之外试用。
items.summary_en: A solo developer's Show HN. Instead of picking one model, Echo treats a pool of open-weight models (GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.7, and others) as a single system. It started from an experiment: if for each problem you knew in advance which models would help and how to combine their outputs, that “oracle” ensemble would massively beat any single model in the pool — but you can't deploy it, because it relies on information you only have after the fact. Echo tries to recover part of that edge without hindsight: per request it computes how much compute to spend, which models take part, and how to combine their outputs. A finding that surprised the author is how complementary the models are — a model that's clearly weaker overall is still very useful on a particular class of problem, or as one piece of a combination. On his first eval mix, Echo beat the best single model in the pool and matched the aggregate quality of Fable, his stronger comparison system, at about a third of the cost. He's candid about the limits: it sometimes mis-allocates compute or mis-combines; and coding and agentic tasks are harder because the quality of each decision is harder to measure. He ships a chat UI and an OpenAI-compatible API so it can be tried outside the eval setup.
items.why: 本期成本和 GTM 的主打内容之一，直接为一版行动提供素材。可迁移的关键洞见不是“路由到最便宜的模型”（这已是过去式），而是一组互补的廉价开源模型，只要调度得当，就能媲美前沿系统。价值在于分工和拼接这一层，而非任何单一模型——这正是社评的重点之一。对独立开发者而言，它提供了一个今晚就能启动的成本节约实验。需要注意：数字为作者自测，方法可借鉴，但数字需打折扣。
items.why_en: One of the issue's cost/GTM anchors, feeding Action 1 directly. The transferable insight isn't “route to the cheapest” (that was yesterday) but that a set of complementary cheap open-weight models, orchestrated well, can match a frontier system — the value is the allocation-and-combination layer, not any one model, which is one of the editorial's landing points. For solo builders it offers a money-saving experiment you can start tonight. Read with the flag: the numbers are self-reported — borrow the method, discount the figure.

items.title: OneCLI：给 AI agent 用的开源密钥网关，别把真凭证交到它手里
items.title_en: Show HN: OneCLI — an open-source credential gateway that keeps secrets out of AI agents
items.author: OneCLI（Jonathan & Guy）· Hacker News
items.summary: 两位安全背景的创始人发布了 Show HN。他们在自己的开源数据库工具 ChartDB 上使用 agent 时遇到了一个问题：传统密钥库将真实密钥交给调用者，并信任对方妥善保管；但对于 agent，这种方式不适用——你不知道 agent 拿到密钥后做了什么、存储在哪里，甚至可能被诱导交出密钥。OneCLI 的做法是在 agent 和它要调用的服务之间架设一个网络网关：根据 host/path 匹配请求，确认 agent 拥有权限，在最后一跳才将请求中的占位符替换为真实密钥并转发出去，整个过程中 agent 只接触到占位符，不接触真实凭证。密钥要么加密存储在 OneCLI 自己的库中，要么实时从 Bitwarden、1Password 等工具获取。项目已开源。评论区提到有类似工具（如 Infisical），并讨论了目标用户到底是个人开发者、小创业公司，还是寻求此类方案的大企业。
items.summary_en: A Show HN from two founders with security backgrounds. Orchestrating agents on top of their open-source database tool, ChartDB, they hit a problem: a traditional vault hands the real secret to whoever asks and trusts them to keep it safe — but that breaks for an agent, since you don't know what it did with the secret, where it stored it, or whether it can be talked into handing it over. OneCLI puts a network gateway between the agent and the services it calls: it matches each request by host/path, confirms the agent is allowed, and only at the last hop swaps the placeholder in the request for the real secret before forwarding — the agent only ever sees placeholders and never touches the real credential. Secrets sit encrypted in OneCLI's own vault or are pulled live from Bitwarden or 1Password. The project is open source. Commenters mention similar tools (Infisical) and ask whether the target user is solo devs, small startups, or the enterprises that shop for this.
items.why: 本期 agent 安全线，直接为二版行动提供素材，主题上与其他几条区分开。核心判断很实在：给予 agent 的权限越大，风险就越集中在凭证上，而正确的解法是架构性的——不要将真实密钥交给 agent，而是给它一个受控的占位符。这为社评中“一路都得有人把关”的观点补充了凭证边界这一环，也是“模型外面那层工程”的一个具体侧面。
items.why_en: The issue's agent-security thread, feeding Action 2 directly and distinct in theme from the rest. The transferable judgment is concrete: the more autonomy you give an agent, the more the risk concentrates on credentials, and the right fix is architectural — don't hand the agent the real secret, hand it a gated placeholder. It supplies the credential-boundary piece of the editorial's “someone checking all the way through,” and it's one concrete face of the “engineering layer around the model.”

items.title: 走进「模型工厂」：Poolside 如何做到八周量产一个模型
items.title_en: Inside the Model Factory — Eiso Kant, Poolside AI
items.author: Latent Space（swyx & Vibhu 对谈 Eiso Kant）
items.author_en: Latent Space (swyx & Vibhu with Eiso Kant)
items.summary: Latent Space 对 Poolside 联合创始人 Eiso Kant 的深度访谈。Poolside 新发布的开源权重模型 Laguna S 2.1，性能超过了 Thinking Machines 近期一个体量约十倍于它的发布；其技术报告因细节扎实而广受好评。访谈的核心是 Poolside 的“模型工厂”：一套端到端的工程系统，能将一个模型从预训练做到发布仅需约八周，不到 70 名研究员每月运行一到两万次实验，数据直接流式输入训练，使用低精度算力，并且 agent 越来越多地负责编写代码、发起任务、评估结果，甚至改动训练下一代模型的流水线本身。Kant 的几条主线：构建模型归根到底是九分工程，而非原始智能；持续性、可验证性、可回溯性，可能比纯粹的聪明更重要；强化学习会更早地进入预训练阶段；下一个 token 预测从互联网中提取的信息还太少；他强调“模型与工具协同设计”，并直言 MCP 和传统工具调用“很蠢”。策略与经济方面：他在市场尚未关注时，花了四年、一千两百万美元押注代码模型这条路；ChatGPT 的出现让他感到被验证，也促使 Poolside 回归开源；他区分了“发布开源权重”和“发表真正开放的研究”这两件事；他刻意将研究团队设在湾区人才竞争之外；最新融资五亿美元；他还表示，即使 Poolside 是幸存的那五家之一，他也宁愿生活在一个存在一百家基础模型公司的世界，而非只有五家的寡头格局。
items.summary_en: Latent Space's long interview with Poolside co-founder Eiso Kant. Poolside's new open-weight model, Laguna S 2.1, beats a recent Thinking Machines release roughly ten times its size, and its tech report drew praise for its detail. The core is Poolside's “Model Factory”: an end-to-end engineering system that takes a model from pre-training to release in about eight weeks, with fewer than 70 researchers running ten to twenty thousand experiments a month, data streamed directly into training, low-precision compute, and agents that increasingly write code, launch jobs, evaluate results, and even modify the pipelines that train the next model. Kant's throughlines: building models is ultimately ninety percent engineering, not raw intelligence; persistence, verification, and backtracking may matter more than sheer smarts; RL will move earlier into pre-training; next-token prediction still extracts too little from the web; and he stresses “model-harness co-design,” calling MCP and traditional tool calls “stupid.” On strategy and economics: he spent four years and $12M on the code-model bet before the market cared; ChatGPT felt like vindication and pulled Poolside back to open source; he distinguishes releasing open weights from publishing genuinely open research; he deliberately built a research org outside the Bay Area talent war; a $500M raise; and he says he'd rather live in a world with a hundred foundation-model companies than five, even if Poolside were one of the five.
items.why: 本期头条的反面印证，也为三版行动提供素材。头条讲“软件工厂”搬给 AI 写业务代码为何失败，而 Poolside 的“模型工厂”却活得很好，恰恰因为它遵循纪律严明的工程原则：可复现的实验、可验证、模型与工具协同设计。同一道理从另一个角度阐述，价值在于那套工程系统，而非模型本身。对 Zen 而言，“一百家还是五家、开源权重作为杠杆”这一框架可直接用于策略判断，而“让每次实验可复现”这一条，也能直接迁移到他日常工作如调整提示词和 agent 的过程中。
items.why_en: The mirror-image proof of the lead, and it feeds Action 3. Where the lead explains why a “software factory” for business code collapses without discipline, Poolside's “Model Factory” is alive precisely because it's disciplined engineering: reproducible experiments, verification, model-harness co-design. The same lesson from the other side — the value is the engineering system, not the model itself. For Zen, the “a hundred labs or five / open weights as leverage” framing is directly usable for strategy, and the “make every experiment reproducible” habit ports straight into his own prompt- and agent-tuning.

notes: 云端无头运行（GitHub Actions，America/New_York，2026-07-24）：本期由两条无头渠道独立凑齐——Hacker News（扫描头版约 60 条，选取 AI/LLM/agent/开发工具/独立建设相关高分帖，逐条进入原文与评论核实）与“文摘”（Latent Space 的 Poolside 长访谈，经 RSS 全文读取）。两平台达标（≥2 来源、5 条），故 partial=false，无缺席横幅。头条《为什么软件工厂会失灵》以作者原文（humanlayer 仓库 wsff.md）通读核对，并按其自陈的商业利益取向与所引 Faros 报告仅为相关性信号加了 flag。刻意避开昨日已覆盖的条目（雅可比反例、Cactus 信心探针、AI 菜单、Ramp Router、pelicanmaxxing），也把主题从昨日的“生成变便宜、判断力变稀缺”挪到今天更具体的一面：判断力落到实处，就是模型外面那套工程纪律，保证跨期多样性。

头版要图：因 YouTube 缩略图不可达，选用 Wikimedia Commons 上一张公有领域照片——1913 年福特高地公园工厂的流水线（restored 版，美国国会图书馆），本地下载到 digests/img/2026-07-24.jpg（same-origin，避免 html2canvas 导出被跨域污染）。选它因为“软件工厂”一词与工业流水线同源，正对头条主题。

OTA：读台账后确认，最近八条——二元评测、按努力档升级、弃权门、多供应商 fail over、成本诊断、按角色分档、能力隔离的评测门、滚动窗口 bandit 路由——全默认“每个子任务都有一条快而可靠的评测线可卡”。今天头条戳穿这个前提：对架构、接口、可维护性这类最值钱的活，根本没有快评测线（RLVR 只奖励测试通过、不惩罚坏设计）。合成新增能力“无快评测则前置对齐（先分流，再上阶梯）”：在整条阶梯最前面加一道分流，先判断子任务的真实质量有没有快评测线，有就照旧上阶梯，没有（设计/可维护性/品味）就别 loopmaxx，先出一份便宜的规划产物、在生成前让人或强规划模型审一遍。它补上 07-18“二元评测”默认好评测已存在的缺口，与 07-19 晚弃权门互补。因云端不能改~/.claude，已作为 proposed（cloud）追加进 ota-ledger.md，交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地为记忆更新。
